description: Nakamura constructs a positive genus-two relation of type (10,10) from three (4,3) copies and a lantern substitution. Its 20 curve factors are not yet encoded as checked braids. No section is certified; minimality excludes a section of square -1.

sections.Surface and conventions: A closed genus-two fiber with ten nonseparating and ten separating positive Dehn twists.
sections.Derivation: Nakamura, Section 3, combines three copies of Hamada's (4,3) factorization through twisted fiber sums and Hurwitz moves, then replaces a four-twist lantern subword with three twists. He proves the resulting total space simply connected and minimal.
sections.Braid factorization: Nakamura's explicit factors are given as Dehn twists about curves and their conjugates. Exact six-strand support words and an independent product certificate have not yet been entered in this package.
sections.Planar mapping class diagrams: The source illustrates the genus-two curves and the lantern. Package support drawings for this relation remain pending.
sections.Standard mapping classes: The source relation has twenty positive factors: ten nonseparating and ten separating twists.
sections.Equivalences and transformations: The source traces its factorization through fiber sums, Hurwitz moves, and one lantern substitution. General lantern or boundary-framed substitutions are not implemented for this example in the package.
sections.Sections and multisections: No section has been certified for Nakamura's (10,10) factorization. The source proves the total space minimal, so it cannot contain a section of self-intersection -1. Other section squares remain open here.
